title: Ordinary coefficient comparison through a locally closed immersion
statement: Over the finite-field datum, for a quasi-compact finite-type X over its separably closed field, a closed immersion g:Z to X, an open immersion j:S to Z, positive coefficient levels m<=n and a bounded constructible finite-Tor Q on S, the published ordinaryComparison from scalar extension of Rg_*Rj_* Q to Rg_*Rj_* of scalar extension Q is invertible.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Ordinary coefficient comparison through a locally closed immersion

proof.text: X is Noetherian and quasi-compact, as is its closed subscheme Z. The open S is Noetherian, hence the open immersion j is quasi-compact. Thus j followed by g is separated and finite type, and S is quasi-compact finite type over the field. The target coefficient ring is finite, hence a finite module for the reduction algebra. Apply finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap_isIso to Q and the composite. Use finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap_comp to identify the factorization up to the two canonical compositors. Both compositors are isomorphisms, so cancel them to obtain invertibility of ordinaryComparison.

theorem locallyClosedOrdinaryComparison_isIso
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (n m : ℕ+) (hmn : m ≤ n) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    {S Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion g]
    (j : S ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (Q : DerivedCategoryModule (coefficient l E n) S)
    (hQ : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E n n.property S Q) :
    IsIso (ordinaryComparison (reduction l E n m hmn) g j Q)
